rows.label: The seven filings and releases are enough for the selected financial, business and evidence-trace work. The set has gaps in legal documents, in the pending acquisition papers and in segment comparability across periods.
Filed statements, debt notes, liquidity text and compliance statements are located for the latest quarter and the prior year end.
A pending refinery acquisition with new financing and a minimum cash requirement is described only in the latest quarterly report and its release.
The segment structure changed from three segments in the annual report to two in 2026 quarterly reports.
Debt totals differ by presentation between the notes, the discussion section and the release.

tables.title: Coverage of evidence demanded by the selected work — Evidence need

rows.label: Statements: balance sheet, operations, equity, cash flows
Debt by instrument with coupon and maturity
Facility capacity, borrowings, letters of credit, availability
Liquidity and minimum cash related to the acquisition
Covenant test terms, thresholds and headroom
Cash paid for interest and taxes

No executed legal documents (indentures, ABL credit agreements, CVR Partners credit agreement) are supplied; the context records legal documents as none. Covenant terms, baskets, springing tests, guarantee releases and security are known only from filing summaries (annual report page:152 to page:159).
Covenant test levels, step-downs and the issuer-reported fixed charge ratio are not located. Compliance is stated, thresholds are not.

Acquisition papers are not supplied: Purchase Agreement, debt commitment letter, subscription agreements, the permanent financing terms. Terms rest on the Q3 report page:11 to page:13 and the Q3 release. The acquisition is pending and not closed at the cutoff.
No presentations or investor decks are supplied. The pack holds earnings releases only, so no slide coverage is claimed.
Segment re-cut: annual report uses three segments, 2026 reports use two. FY2025 segment data in the annual report is not recast in the supplied annual report.
Debt presentation bases differ between note 6, the liquidity discussion table and the release (see conflicts).
Discrete Q4 2025 is not reported in the supplied set; a last-twelve-months view needs derivation from the annual report and the interim periods, on mixed segment bases.

Extraction fidelity: all sources are text extractions. Tables are flattened and column alignment was not checked against the rendered documents. Images and charts were not inspected. Q1 release chunk 1 holds only the extraction header.
Ratings, market quotes, peer data and sponsor materials are blank in the context.
Interim Chief Financial Officer and a separate chief accounting officer certification appear in the Q3 report (page:64, page:71). This is a governance observation, not a source defect.

limitations: Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable. Reported statements for the annual report and the three 2026 quarters give consistent debt, cash and facility data, and the consolidated Adjusted EBITDA bridge ties to net income in every period checked. On a trailing basis to Q3 2026, gross debt is about two times Adjusted EBITDA, net debt is about half a turn, and cash interest is covered about seven times. All three are far better than at FY2025 because trailing Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled, not because debt fell: total debt including finance leases moved little across the four balance sheet dates. The February 2026 refinancing cleared the 2027 term loan and the 2029 notes and pushed the first principal maturity to 2028. Three limits govern use. First, the ratios are on the consolidated perimeter, which includes the CVR Partners entity, its cash and its secured notes. Second, the trailing figure includes a quarter that management calls its best in company history, so the ratio shows capacity at current cracks and not a through-cycle level. Third, none of the ratios includes the pending acquisition, its bridge or its equity, and the target's earnings are not supplied. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable.

facts.label: Definition review
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA is management's measure: EBITDA less favorable changes in the RFS obligation, plus unrealized derivative losses, adjusted for inventory valuation impacts (10-Q Q3 page:56; 10-K page:115). Three points matter for credit use. The RFS adjustment removes the 2025 and 2026 waiver gains (the 2026 waiver is described at about 253 and the 2025 waiver at about 488), so the measure is conservative on that item, but it also removes ongoing RFS revaluation. The derivative add-back of 278 for nine months 2026 removes mark-to-market losses on crack spread swaps while the derivative liabilities of 160 current and 18 long-term remain on the balance sheet, so a cash settlement against those positions is not in Adjusted EBITDA. The inventory valuation line removes a favorable 173 in nine months 2026 on a FIFO basis. Reported EBITDA, trailing, is 964 against 919 adjusted, and leverage on the reported basis would be lower, but the reported figure includes the waiver gains. Cash interest cover is computed on Adjusted EBITDA only. Covenant EBITDA is not defined in the supplied text; the covenant basis differs from this measure and is Not supplied.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: CVR Energy is a controlled holding company with two operating legs. The Petroleum segment runs two mid-continent refineries, Coffeyville in Kansas and Wynnewood in Oklahoma, supported by crude gathering and logistics. The Nitrogen Fertilizer segment is CVR Partners, which the parent consolidates with about 37 percent of the units and all of the general partner. Earnings are driven by refined product margins against crude cost, by the cost of complying with the Renewable Fuel Standard and by fertilizer prices and plant utilization. The latest quarter was exceptionally strong, which management attributes to the conflict in the Middle East and to a regulatory waiver; both are external and reversible. On November 2, 2026, after the balance sheet date, the company signed an agreement to buy two refineries and related assets from Marathon Petroleum for about 4.2 billion in cash. The agreement is pending regulatory clearance, is to be financed by new secured debt, a bridge facility if needed, an enlarged asset based loan and preferred and common equity commitments, and carries a minimum cash condition and termination fees. For a creditor, the transaction is the dominant fact: it would roughly change the scale of the business, add substantial secured debt ahead of existing unsecured notes, and rests on documents and target earnings that are not in the source set. Governance is concentrated in Icahn Enterprises, which both controls the company and has committed equity to the acquisition. The standalone credit profile in the prior module is therefore a starting point, not the post-transaction picture.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Pending acquisition. On November 2, 2026 the company entered into an equity and asset purchase agreement with indirect subsidiaries and affiliates of Marathon Petroleum Corporation to acquire the St. Paul Park refinery in Minnesota, the Mandan refinery in North Dakota, a 17 percent interest in each of Minnesota Pipe Line Company and MPL Investments, and associated wholesale marketing and logistics assets, assuming certain liabilities, for aggregate cash consideration of approximately 4.2 billion, subject to working capital and inventory adjustments. It is a Documentary Fact in the third quarter 10-Q, accounted for as a business combination with the company as acquirer, not closed at the cutoff, and a subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. Closing needs expiry of the antitrust waiting period and other approvals. Management expects closing before the end of 2026 (Management Language), while the risk factors state the outside date is 270 days after signing, extendable to 360 days in specified circumstances. A termination fee of 6%, 4% or 2% of the aggregate base purchase price applies depending on the circumstances; the dollar amounts are Not supplied because the base price is not separately stated from the cash consideration.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Financing. The company intends to fund the purchase with cash on hand, borrowings under its asset based loan, new senior secured debt (the permanent financing), the equity investments and the proceeds of a registered common stock offering. A debt commitment letter from Barclays Bank PLC and others provides a 364-day senior secured bridge loan of up to 2.5 billion to the extent permanent financing proceeds fall short, and consents to raise the asset based loan commitments by 550 to 1.1 billion at closing, or alternatively a new 1.1 billion facility refinancing the existing one. A commercial counterparty has committed to buy 800 million of non-voting common equivalent convertible preferred stock at closing. Icahn Enterprises committed up to 500 million of equity at the same price per share, terminating on completion of a common offering of at least 500 million. The company must hold at least 500 million of unrestricted cash until closing or termination, rising by up to 500 million of equity offering proceeds. Affiliates of the commercial counterparty will also supply crude, take product offtake and purchase initial crude and feedstock inventories at the two target refineries for ten years from closing, which is both a funding and a supply-side link. The size of the permanent financing, the total sources and uses and the target's earnings are Not supplied, so pro forma leverage and interest cover are Not calculable. The sum of committed sources cannot be compared with uses from the supplied text.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Creditor reading (Analyst Interpretation). Existing senior notes are unsecured; new financing is described as senior secured and an enlarged secured asset based loan ranks ahead of them on shared collateral, so effective subordination of the existing unsecured holders would rise on closing. Equity of 800 plus up to 500 reduces but does not remove the debt need. The 500 minimum cash and the bridge's 364-day tenor make the permanent financing market a near-term event. These are mechanics, not a view on outcome.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues in 2026. On February 12, 2026 the company issued 1 billion of notes, 600 of 7.500 percent senior notes due February 2031 and 400 of 7.875 percent senior notes due February 2034, with net proceeds of 993. Proceeds repaid the petroleum term loan, redeemed all 8.500 percent notes due 2029 at 104.250 percent of principal (a loss on extinguishment of 28 in interest expense) and redeemed 217 of the 5.750 percent notes due 2028 at par, leaving 183. On the same date the asset based loan was amended to raise commitments from 345 to 550, extend maturity from June 2027 to February 2031 and change the borrowing base and negative covenants. The effect was to push the first principal maturity to 2028 and to extend the maturity profile, with a changed coupon mix. The 6.125 percent senior secured notes of CVR Partners due June 2028 were not changed. Guarantee text for the new notes is in the 10-K and excludes CVR Partners and its subsidiaries.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: CVR Energy's standalone credit position is strong today, but the view for creditors depends on a pending debt-funded acquisition and on cycle-high earnings. The strongest support is the balance sheet at September 30, 2026: total debt of USD 1,781 million against trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 919 million, or 1.94x gross and 0.55x net, liquidity of USD 1,853 million and no note principal due before 2028. The weakest point is that earnings are at a cyclical high from elevated crack spreads and regulatory waivers, while the acquisition for about USD 4.2 billion in cash, with a bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion, is not in any ratio. What decides the outcome is the permanent financing structure, the target refineries' earnings and whether current margins last.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage has improved through earnings, not repayment. CVR Energy's total debt including finance leases moved from USD 1,765 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,781 million at September 30, 2026, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 393 million to USD 919 million, taking gross leverage from 4.49x to 1.94x and net leverage from 3.19x to 0.55x. Because the improvement comes from the numerator, a normalization of crack spreads would move these ratios back toward the earlier levels, which is why the debt levels, not the ratios, are the steadier anchor. [Financial base; Business context, market drivers]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, the maturity and liquidity position is comfortable on a standalone basis. The February 2026 refinancing repaid the term loan, redeemed the 2029 notes and part of the 2028 notes, and moved the first principal maturity to 2028, when USD 733 million falls due (USD 183 million at CVR Energy and USD 550 million of secured notes at CVR Partners). Cash was USD 1,278 million and undrawn facilities USD 575 million, for USD 1,853 million, but USD 158 million of the cash sits in the consolidated CVR Partners entity and USD 500 million must stay unrestricted until the acquisition closes or the agreement ends, so usable liquidity is lower than the headline. [Financial base liquidity and maturities; Business context transaction summary]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, the pending acquisition is the dominant credit event. On November 2, 2026, after the balance sheet date, CVR Energy agreed to buy two refineries and related logistics from Marathon Petroleum for about USD 4.2 billion in cash. The committed funding includes a senior secured bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion, a USD 550 million increase in the asset based loan to USD 1.1 billion, USD 800 million of convertible preferred stock from a commercial counterparty and up to USD 500 million from Icahn Enterprises. Because new debt is described as senior secured and the asset based loan is secured, existing unsecured noteholders would be effectively subordinated to a larger secured pool after closing. The permanent financing size, the target's earnings and total sources and uses are not supplied, so no post-closing ratio can be stated. [Business context transaction summary and gaps]

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Low standalone leverage (Documentary Fact): total debt of USD 1,781 million over trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 919 million gives 1.94x gross and 0.55x net, which leaves capacity to absorb a margin downturn before leverage returns to the FY2025 level of 4.49x. Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact): USD 1,853 million of liquidity, undrawn asset based facilities (USD 20 million of letters of credit issued against the CVR Energy facility), and no note principal due before 2028. Cash generation (Documentary Fact): nine months 2026 free cash flow after capital expenditure and turnaround of USD 872 million against negative USD 238 million in FY2025, which provided the cash build. Sponsor funding support (Analyst Interpretation): the Icahn Enterprises commitment of up to USD 500 million of equity at a third party's price aligns the controlling holder with closing and reduces the debt required. Regional logistics advantage (Documentary Fact): the company gathers about 67 percent and 94 percent of the crude for Coffeyville and Wynnewood.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Cyclical, elevated earnings (Management Language carried, Analyst Interpretation on effect): management ties the margin improvement to the Iran war and calls the third quarter its best in company history; trailing figures include a quarter that is not a through-cycle level, so leverage is understated relative to mid-cycle. Pending acquisition (Documentary Fact): about USD 4.2 billion in cash, financed by new secured debt, a bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion and equity of USD 800 million plus up to USD 500 million; post-closing metrics are Not calculable and secured debt would rank ahead of the existing unsecured notes. Regulatory and hedge exposure (Documentary Fact): an accrued RFS obligation of USD 230 million under court challenge, derivative liabilities and a large Adjusted EBITDA add-back for unrealized hedge losses. Concentration (Documentary Fact): two refineries in one region, one top petroleum customer at about 12 percent of segment sales and fertilizer top two customers at about 28 percent. Structure and control (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on control): about USD 569 million of consolidated debt sits at CVR Partners and its USD 158 million of cash is not freely available to the parent; the controlling holder can direct strategic transactions, and covenant terms are Not supplied. Management transition (Documentary Fact): chief executive change in June 2026 and an interim chief financial officer during a large transaction.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that nine-month 2026 free cash flow of 872 and trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 919 are real cash and earnings, that debt is little changed, that no note principal is due before 2028, and that the controlling holder has committed equity. The evidence against a comfortable reading is that the improvement comes from the numerator. What would make the supportive case win: a permanent financing and equity package that holds post-closing leverage near the standalone level, clearance of the antitrust review, and margins staying above mid-cycle through the first quarters after closing. Downside chain with observable triggers: the initiating condition is a normalization of crack spreads or an end to Middle East supply disruption, which cuts refining margin per barrel first, then Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow; the financial transmission is a return of leverage toward the FY2025 level (4.53x on current debt in the CP-2 sensitivity), with RFS purchases, derivative settlements and tax payments drawing on the 1,853 of liquidity; the refinancing consequence is the 364-day bridge and the 733 maturing in 2028. ### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for source sufficiency only. The annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases are all filed or furnished primary documents of one registrant, CVR Energy, Inc., and every period between FY2025 and Q3 2026 is covered by a located filing. That is enough for the owners of CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 to perform their methods. No source is blocked and no consumer is CONDITIONAL. The limitations are bounded and listed below: no executed legal documents, no acquisition agreement or financing commitment papers, no presentations, a segment re-cut between the annual and quarterly reports, differing debt presentation bases, and an extraction that was not reviewed for fidelity. This is not a statement that downstream analysis is complete, and the assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED.

### Conflicts and comparability issues

1. Segment structure. The annual report says "three reportable segments: petroleum, renewables, and nitrogen fertilizer" (annual report page:88). The 2026 quarterly reports say "two reportable segments: Petroleum and Nitrogen Fertilizer" (Q3 report page:26), and the annual report anticipated the change ("This reversion is expected to result in changes to the Company's reportable segments in 2026", annual report page:175). Downstream effect: FY2025 segment figures from the annual report are not on the same basis as 2025 comparatives in the 2026 quarterly reports, where renewable fuel activity sits in "Other". CP-1 must label the basis and not splice them.

2. Debt presentation. The note 6 total for CVR Energy debt includes finance lease obligations ("Total CVR Energy debt 1,175 999", Q3 report page:16) while the liquidity discussion table excludes them ("Total CVR Energy debt 1,171 997", Q3 report page:59). The release rounds ("including $570 million held by the Nitrogen Fertilizer Segment", Q3 release page:2) against the note ("Total Nitrogen Fertilizer Segment debt 569 569", Q3 report page:16). These are basis and rounding differences, not contradictions of fact, but any leverage or maturity work must name its basis.
3. Management language. The Q3 release calls the quarter "the best quarterly results in the Company's history" (Q3 release page:1). That is management characterisation and is not adopted here.
4. The Q3 report cover page states shares outstanding at October 30, 2026, and the signature is dated November 3, 2026. Both are inside the cutoff.

### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Debt is low against trailing Adjusted EBITDA, 1.94x gross and 0.55x net at the latest quarter, with liquidity of 1,853 million. The ratios exclude the pending acquisition financing and rest on a management EBITDA measure. | Medium | Covenant levels, the acquisition financing terms and the sustainability of the current earnings level are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from 393 million in FY2025 to 919 million, while total debt moved only from 1,765 million to 1,781 million. | Gross leverage fell from 4.49x to 1.94x; earnings level, not debt reduction, drove the change. | Medium |

| Cash rose to 1,278 million, including 158 million held in the consolidated CVR Partners entity, and 500 million must stay unrestricted until the acquisition closes. | Usable liquidity is lower than the headline figure of 1,853 million. | Medium |

| The 2026 refinancing replaced the 2029 notes and term loan with 2031 and 2034 notes; no note principal falls due before 2028. | Near-term maturity risk is low; 733 million falls due in 2028. | High |

| Claims outside debt grew: the RFS obligation, derivative liabilities and accrued income taxes sit in other current liabilities. | These near-term cash calls draw on the same liquidity and are not in net debt. | Medium |

| Adjusted EBITDA adds back unrealized derivative losses and removes RFS changes, so reported EBITDA of 964 million trailing differs from 919 million. | Definition choice moves leverage and cover; the basis must be named whenever a ratio is used. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is usable. Reported statements for the annual report and the three 2026 quarters give consistent debt, cash and facility data, and the consolidated Adjusted EBITDA bridge ties to net income in every period checked. On a trailing basis to Q3 2026, gross debt is about two times Adjusted EBITDA, net debt is about half a turn, and cash interest is covered about seven times. All three are far better than at FY2025 because trailing Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled, not because debt fell: total debt including finance leases moved little across the four balance sheet dates. The February 2026 refinancing cleared the 2027 term loan and the 2029 notes and pushed the first principal maturity to 2028. Three limits govern use. First, the ratios are on the consolidated perimeter, which includes the CVR Partners entity, its cash and its secured notes. Second, the trailing figure includes a quarter that management calls its best in company history, so the ratio shows capacity at current cracks and not a through-cycle level. Third, none of the ratios includes the pending acquisition, its bridge or its equity, and the target's earnings are not supplied. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable.

Three points matter for credit use. The RFS adjustment removes the 2025 and 2026 waiver gains (the 2026 waiver is described at about 253 and the 2025 waiver at about 488), so the measure is conservative on that item, but it also removes ongoing RFS revaluation. The derivative add-back of 278 for nine months 2026 removes mark-to-market losses on crack spread swaps while the derivative liabilities of 160 current and 18 long-term remain on the balance sheet, so a cash settlement against those positions is not in Adjusted EBITDA. The inventory valuation line removes a favorable 173 in nine months 2026 on a FIFO basis. Reported EBITDA, trailing, is 964 against 919 adjusted, and leverage on the reported basis would be lower, but the reported figure includes the waiver gains. Cash interest cover is computed on Adjusted EBITDA only. Covenant EBITDA is not defined in the supplied text; the covenant basis differs from this measure and is Not supplied.

CP-0's note that the release rounds segment debt to 570 against the note's 569 is not used here; the note value governs. No CP-0 statement is corrected.

The cutoff is 2026-11-05. The question is which transaction, ownership, business and operating facts matter most to a creditor, with evidence, risk mechanic and credit implication for each material conclusion. The perimeter is CVR Energy, Inc. consolidated, a holding company that owns the petroleum refining business directly and controls CVR Partners, LP, a listed partnership that makes nitrogen fertilizer and is consolidated as a variable interest entity.

Each fact row carries one category: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| A mid-continent refiner and fertilizer holding company controlled by Icahn Enterprises has agreed to a large refinery acquisition that is not yet closed and will be debt and equity funded. Current earnings are cycle-high. | Medium | The acquisition papers, target earnings and permanent financing terms are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The agreed acquisition of two Marathon refineries for about 4.2 billion in cash is pending, with a bridge of up to 2.5 billion committed. | Leverage and liquidity after closing are unknown and would differ materially from the standalone figures. | Medium |

| Icahn Enterprises owns about 71 percent of the stock, and the company is a controlled company. | Control sits with one holder who also commits equity funding; creditor protection rests on documents not supplied. | High |

| Third quarter earnings reflect elevated crack spreads after the Iran war and a regulatory waiver. | Cash generation is strong but tied to cyclical margins and regulatory decisions that can reverse. | Medium |
| The chief executive changed in mid-2026 and the chief financial officer role is held on an interim basis. | Management continuity during a large acquisition is a monitoring point. | Medium |
| Nitrogen fertilizer sits in a separate listed partnership with its own secured notes. | Cash at that entity is not freely available to the parent. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

CVR Energy is a controlled holding company with two operating legs. The Petroleum segment runs two mid-continent refineries, Coffeyville in Kansas and Wynnewood in Oklahoma, supported by crude gathering and logistics. The Nitrogen Fertilizer segment is CVR Partners, which the parent consolidates with about 37 percent of the units and all of the general partner. Earnings are driven by refined product margins against crude cost, by the cost of complying with the Renewable Fuel Standard and by fertilizer prices and plant utilization. The latest quarter was exceptionally strong, which management attributes to the conflict in the Middle East and to a regulatory waiver; both are external and reversible. On November 2, 2026, after the balance sheet date, the company signed an agreement to buy two refineries and related assets from Marathon Petroleum for about 4.2 billion in cash. The agreement is pending regulatory clearance, is to be financed by new secured debt, a bridge facility if needed, an enlarged asset based loan and preferred and common equity commitments, and carries a minimum cash condition and termination fees. For a creditor, the transaction is the dominant fact: it would roughly change the scale of the business, add substantial secured debt ahead of existing unsecured notes, and rests on documents and target earnings that are not in the source set. Governance is concentrated in Icahn Enterprises, which both controls the company and has committed equity to the acquisition. The standalone credit profile in the prior module is therefore a starting point, not the post-transaction picture.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Pending acquisition. On November 2, 2026 the company entered into an equity and asset purchase agreement with indirect subsidiaries and affiliates of Marathon Petroleum Corporation to acquire the St. Paul Park refinery in Minnesota, the Mandan refinery in North Dakota, a 17 percent interest in each of Minnesota Pipe Line Company and MPL Investments, and associated wholesale marketing and logistics assets, assuming certain liabilities, for aggregate cash consideration of approximately 4.2 billion, subject to working capital and inventory adjustments. It is a Documentary Fact in the third quarter 10-Q, accounted for as a business combination with the company as acquirer, not closed at the cutoff, and a subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. Closing needs expiry of the antitrust waiting period and other approvals. Management expects closing before the end of 2026 (Management Language), while the risk factors state the outside date is 270 days after signing, extendable to 360 days in specified circumstances. A termination fee of 6%, 4% or 2% of the aggregate base purchase price applies depending on the circumstances; the dollar amounts are Not supplied because the base price is not separately stated from the cash consideration.

Financing. The company intends to fund the purchase with cash on hand, borrowings under its asset based loan, new senior secured debt (the permanent financing), the equity investments and the proceeds of a registered common stock offering. A debt commitment letter from Barclays Bank PLC and others provides a 364-day senior secured bridge loan of up to 2.5 billion to the extent permanent financing proceeds fall short, and consents to raise the asset based loan commitments by 550 to 1.1 billion at closing, or alternatively a new 1.1 billion facility refinancing the existing one. A commercial counterparty has committed to buy 800 million of non-voting common equivalent convertible preferred stock at closing. Icahn Enterprises committed up to 500 million of equity at the same price per share, terminating on completion of a common offering of at least 500 million. The company must hold at least 500 million of unrestricted cash until closing or termination, rising by up to 500 million of equity offering proceeds. Affiliates of the commercial counterparty will also supply crude, take product offtake and purchase initial crude and feedstock inventories at the two target refineries for ten years from closing, which is both a funding and a supply-side link. The size of the permanent financing, the total sources and uses and the target's earnings are Not supplied, so pro forma leverage and interest cover are Not calculable. The sum of committed sources cannot be compared with uses from the supplied text.

Creditor reading (Analyst Interpretation). Existing senior notes are unsecured; new financing is described as senior secured and an enlarged secured asset based loan ranks ahead of them on shared collateral, so effective subordination of the existing unsecured holders would rise on closing. Equity of 800 plus up to 500 reduces but does not remove the debt need. The 500 minimum cash and the bridge's 364-day tenor make the permanent financing market a near-term event. These are mechanics, not a view on outcome.

New debt issues in 2026. On February 12, 2026 the company issued 1 billion of notes, 600 of 7.500 percent senior notes due February 2031 and 400 of 7.875 percent senior notes due February 2034, with net proceeds of 993. Proceeds repaid the petroleum term loan, redeemed all 8.500 percent notes due 2029 at 104.250 percent of principal (a loss on extinguishment of 28 in interest expense) and redeemed 217 of the 5.750 percent notes due 2028 at par, leaving 183. On the same date the asset based loan was amended to raise commitments from 345 to 550, extend maturity from June 2027 to February 2031 and change the borrowing base and negative covenants. The effect was to push the first principal maturity to 2028 and to extend the maturity profile, with a changed coupon mix. The 6.125 percent senior secured notes of CVR Partners due June 2028 were not changed. Guarantee text for the new notes is in the 10-K and excludes CVR Partners and its subsidiaries.

### Credit view

CVR Energy's standalone credit position is strong today, but the view for creditors depends on a pending debt-funded acquisition and on cycle-high earnings. The strongest support is the balance sheet at September 30, 2026: total debt of USD 1,781 million against trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 919 million, or 1.94x gross and 0.55x net, liquidity of USD 1,853 million and no note principal due before 2028. The weakest point is that earnings are at a cyclical high from elevated crack spreads and regulatory waivers, while the acquisition for about USD 4.2 billion in cash, with a bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion, is not in any ratio. What decides the outcome is the permanent financing structure, the target refineries' earnings and whether current margins last.
### Key findings

First, leverage has improved through earnings, not repayment. CVR Energy's total debt including finance leases moved from USD 1,765 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,781 million at September 30, 2026, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 393 million to USD 919 million, taking gross leverage from 4.49x to 1.94x and net leverage from 3.19x to 0.55x. Because the improvement comes from the numerator, a normalization of crack spreads would move these ratios back toward the earlier levels, which is why the debt levels, not the ratios, are the steadier anchor. [Financial base; Business context, market drivers]

Second, the maturity and liquidity position is comfortable on a standalone basis. The February 2026 refinancing repaid the term loan, redeemed the 2029 notes and part of the 2028 notes, and moved the first principal maturity to 2028, when USD 733 million falls due (USD 183 million at CVR Energy and USD 550 million of secured notes at CVR Partners). Cash was USD 1,278 million and undrawn facilities USD 575 million, for USD 1,853 million, but USD 158 million of the cash sits in the consolidated CVR Partners entity and USD 500 million must stay unrestricted until the acquisition closes or the agreement ends, so usable liquidity is lower than the headline. [Financial base liquidity and maturities; Business context transaction summary]

Third, cash interest cover is high and well above the FY2025 level: trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 6.96x trailing cash interest of USD 132 million, against 2.77x in FY2025. This covers the debt as it stood, including notes issued in February 2026 at 7.500 percent and 7.875 percent; it does not cover acquisition debt. [Financial base interest cover]

Fourth, the pending acquisition is the dominant credit event. On November 2, 2026, after the balance sheet date, CVR Energy agreed to buy two refineries and related logistics from Marathon Petroleum for about USD 4.2 billion in cash. The committed funding includes a senior secured bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion, a USD 550 million increase in the asset based loan to USD 1.1 billion, USD 800 million of convertible preferred stock from a commercial counterparty and up to USD 500 million from Icahn Enterprises. Because new debt is described as senior secured and the asset based loan is secured, existing unsecured noteholders would be effectively subordinated to a larger secured pool after closing. The permanent financing size, the target's earnings and total sources and uses are not supplied, so no post-closing ratio can be stated. [Business context transaction summary and gaps]

Fifth, claims outside debt and the definition of Adjusted EBITDA qualify the headline ratios. At September 30, 2026 the accrued RFS obligation was USD 230 million, derivative liabilities USD 160 million current and USD 18 million long-term, and accrued income taxes USD 132 million, none of which is in total debt, and the December 2025 contractual table showed transportation agreements of USD 995 million and purchase commitments of USD 165 million. Adjusted EBITDA adds back unrealized derivative losses of USD 278 million for nine months 2026 and removes favorable RFS changes, so it differs from reported trailing EBITDA of USD 964 million; the basis must be named whenever a ratio is used. [Financial base claims outside debt and definitions]

Sixth, governance is concentrated and in transition. Icahn Enterprises holds about 71 percent of the stock, the company relies on controlled-company exemptions, a separation and a new employment agreement for the chief executive are dated June 18, 2026, and the chief financial officer role is interim. Control is a funding positive, since Icahn Enterprises committed equity at the same price as a third party, but it also means transactions can be directed by one holder, and the legal protections for creditors sit in documents that are not supplied. [Business context ownership and governance]
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Low standalone leverage (Documentary Fact): total debt of USD 1,781 million over trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 919 million gives 1.94x gross and 0.55x net, which leaves capacity to absorb a margin downturn before leverage returns to the FY2025 level of 4.49x. Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact): USD 1,853 million of liquidity, undrawn asset based facilities (USD 20 million of letters of credit issued against the CVR Energy facility), and no note principal due before 2028. Cash generation (Documentary Fact): nine months 2026 free cash flow after capital expenditure and turnaround of USD 872 million against negative USD 238 million in FY2025, which provided the cash build. Sponsor funding support (Analyst Interpretation): the Icahn Enterprises commitment of up to USD 500 million of equity at a third party's price aligns the controlling holder with closing and reduces the debt required. Regional logistics advantage (Documentary Fact): the company gathers about 67 percent and 94 percent of the crude for Coffeyville and Wynnewood.

Weaknesses. Cyclical, elevated earnings (Management Language carried, Analyst Interpretation on effect): management ties the margin improvement to the Iran war and calls the third quarter its best in company history; trailing figures include a quarter that is not a through-cycle level, so leverage is understated relative to mid-cycle. Pending acquisition (Documentary Fact): about USD 4.2 billion in cash, financed by new secured debt, a bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion and equity of USD 800 million plus up to USD 500 million; post-closing metrics are Not calculable and secured debt would rank ahead of the existing unsecured notes. Regulatory and hedge exposure (Documentary Fact): an accrued RFS obligation of USD 230 million under court challenge, derivative liabilities and a large Adjusted EBITDA add-back for unrealized hedge losses. Concentration (Documentary Fact): two refineries in one region, one top petroleum customer at about 12 percent of segment sales and fertilizer top two customers at about 28 percent. Structure and control (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on control): about USD 569 million of consolidated debt sits at CVR Partners and its USD 158 million of cash is not freely available to the parent; the controlling holder can direct strategic transactions, and covenant terms are Not supplied. Management transition (Documentary Fact): chief executive change in June 2026 and an interim chief financial officer during a large transaction.
### Credit assessment

| Overall fundamental credit view | Strong standalone profile; the creditor view is conditional on acquisition financing and margin durability | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Financial base ratios and liquidity; business context transaction summary and credit translations |

Thesis. CVR Energy's low standalone leverage and large liquidity support its credit today, but cycle-high earnings and a pending debt-funded acquisition under a controlling holder make the post-closing credit profile the deciding question (Analyst Interpretation).

| Governance and transition | About 71 percent held by Icahn Enterprises; new chief executive; interim chief financial officer | Documents that govern creditor protections are not supplied; transition risk during integration | Material |
| Contingent liabilities | Unquantified guaranty dispute, ammonia release suits and 45Q fee guarantee up to USD 45 million | Potential cash claims outside debt | Minor |
| Segment and definition comparability | Three segments in FY2025, two in 2026; management Adjusted EBITDA | Trend analysis needs a stated basis | Minor |

## Calculations
The figures in this module are those settled in the financial base handoff and are not recomputed. The following new sensitivities are shown with their inputs; they are illustrations, not forecasts.

The last two rows are a mechanical bound only: the bridge is drawn only to the extent permanent financing falls short, equity of USD 800 million and up to USD 500 million offsets part of the need, the cash on hand and asset based loan fund part, and the target's earnings are Not supplied. They are not an estimate of post-closing leverage, which is Not calculable. All amounts are USD millions except the multiples.

### Cross-module contradictions

None found. Pairs examined and found consistent: the improvement in leverage in CP-1 against the cautious wording in CP-2 that it came from earnings rather than repayment (total debt moved only from 1,765 to 1,781); strong liquidity in CP-1 against the minimum cash condition and VIE cash in CP-1A and CP-2; the expected closing before the end of 2026 against the 270-day outside date in CP-1A; supportive equity commitment from the controlling holder against the mixed distribution history, both tagged and not netted; the sponsor behaviour table, which finds no priming or extraction, against the absence of indentures, which is carried as a gap rather than as evidence of absence.
### Verdict consistency

The verdicts agree across modules for every shared claim. CP-2's confidence of Medium is no higher than the readiness judgment of ready with limitations allows, and its gaps ledger matches the inherited gaps.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that nine-month 2026 free cash flow of 872 and trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 919 are real cash and earnings, that debt is little changed, that no note principal is due before 2028, and that the controlling holder has committed equity. The evidence against a comfortable reading is that the improvement comes from the numerator. What would make the supportive case win: a permanent financing and equity package that holds post-closing leverage near the standalone level, clearance of the antitrust review, and margins staying above mid-cycle through the first quarters after closing. Downside chain with observable triggers: the initiating condition is a normalization of crack spreads or an end to Middle East supply disruption, which cuts refining margin per barrel first, then Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow; the financial transmission is a return of leverage toward the FY2025 level (4.53x on current debt in the CP-2 sensitivity), with RFS purchases, derivative settlements and tax payments drawing on the 1,853 of liquidity; the refinancing consequence is the 364-day bridge and the 733 maturing in 2028. Triggers to watch: Group 3 crack spreads, RIN prices and the D.C. Circuit outcomes, antitrust clearance, launch and pricing of the permanent financing, and the covenant certificates once obtainable.
